actions.reason: merge() now jumps between occurrences of pair[0] using list.count/list.index (C) and copies the unchanged runs with slices instead of a per-element Python loop. It still replaces greedily from left to right, including when p0==p1. RegexTokenizer.train skips merge for chunks that don't contain pair[0] (they are never mutated, so they are reused). It also counts pairs for weight-1 chunks with _count_elements, which gives the same counts and the same dict insertion order, so ties break the same way. In encode, the min() key lambda no longer looks up self.merges.get or rebuilds float('inf') on every call. Outputs are byte-identical. Measured train_ir at 0.763x and encode_ir at 0.790x.
